questions.question: What is the name of the connective tissue that connects two bones to each other?

__
 
• **Ligaments** are a type of connective tissue that connect bones to other bones in joints.
 
• They are composed of dense, fibrous connective tissue that provides stability and support to joints.
 
• Ligaments are crucial for maintaining the structure of the skeletal system and enabling proper movement.
 
• They contain collagen fibers, which provide tensile strength and elasticity to withstand various types of stresses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tendons**

 
 
• Tendons are connective tissues that connect muscles to bones.
 
• They are composed mainly of collagen fibers and are designed to withstand tension.
 
• Tendons play a vital role in transmitting the force generated by muscles to bones, facilitating movement.
 
 
 
• **Cartilage**
 
 
• Cartilage is a flexible connective tissue found in various parts of the body, including joints, ear, and nose.
 
• It provides cushioning and reduces friction between bones in joints.
 
• There are three types of cartilage: hyaline, elastic, and fibrocartilage, each serving different functions.
 
 
 
• **Adipose Tissue**
 
 
• Adipose tissue, or body fat, is a type of connective tissue that stores energy in the form of fat.
 
• It also provides insulation and cushioning to protect organs and tissues.
 
• Adipose tissue is found beneath the skin, around internal organs, and in bone marrow.
 
 
 
• **Fibrous Connective Tissue**
 
 
• Fibrous connective tissue is characterized by a dense arrangement of collagen fibers.
 
• It includes ligaments, tendons, and the dermis layer of the skin.
 
• This type of tissue provides strength, support, and flexibility to various body structures.

questions.question: Which of the following may be called as fiscal deficit?

options.text: Total expenditure – Total receipts other than borrowings
Revenue expenditure + Capital expenditure − Revenue receipts

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Total expenditure – Total receipts other than borrowings.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• A fiscal Deficit is a difference between the total income of the government (total taxes and non-debt capital receipts) and its total expenditure.
 
• While calculating the total revenue, borrowings are not included. 
 
• Hence, Fiscal Deficit is- Budget expenditure or Total Expenditure- Budget or total receipts excluding borrowings.
 
 
• A fiscal deficit situation occurs when the government’s expenditure exceeds its income.
 
• This difference is calculated both in absolute terms and also as a percentage of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of the country.
 
• A recurring high fiscal deficit means that the government has been spending beyond its means.
 
• The government describes the fiscal deficit of India as “the excess of total disbursements from the Consolidated Fund of India, excluding repayment of the debt, over total receipts into the Fund (excluding the debt receipts) during a financial year”.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

__
 
• What constitutes the government’s total income or receipts?

 
 
• It has two components revenue receipts and non-tax revenues.

 
 
• Revenue receipts of the government

 
 
• Corporation Tax
 
• Income Tax
 
• Custom Duties
 
• Union Excise Duties
 
• GST and taxes of Union territories.
 
 
 
• Non-tax revenues
 
 
• Interest Receipts
 
• Dividends and Profits
 
• External Grants
 
• Other non-tax revenues
 
• Receipts of union territories
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• Expenditures of the government:
 
 
• Revenue Expenditure
 
• Capital Expenditure
 
• Interest Payments
 
• Grants-in-aid for the creation of capital assets
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Fiscal Deficit formula: 

 
 
• Fiscal Deficit = Total expenditure of the government (capital and revenue expenditure) – Total income of the government (Revenue receipts + recovery of loans + other receipts)
 
• If the total expenditure of the government exceeds its total revenue and non-revenue receipts in a financial year, then that gap is the fiscal deficit for the financial year. 
 
• The government meets the fiscal deficit by borrowing money. In a way, the total borrowing requirements of the government in a financial year are equal to the fiscal deficit in that year.
